correctness.rationale: Multiplicativity reduces Rκ(p^a) to the order-(κ−1) power mean Uκ,p(a) of the increasing affine function S_{p,a−1}+t p^(−a), with endpoints geometric and maximum means. The common independent p-adic valuation model P(V_p=a)=(1−1/p)/p^a converges almost surely because ∑ E log Uκ,p(V_p)=O(∑p p^(−2)). The finite-prime CRT limit with a uniform log-tail bound proves integer-sampling weak convergence, and local factors 1+O_z(p^(−2)) yield locally uniformly convergent Mellin products and all real moments; uniform integrability yields mean convergence. An infinite sequence of disjoint prime blocks with absence probability bounded away from 0 and 1, followed by an independent fair-coin representation and Sperner anti-chain bound, forces absence of atoms. Divergence of ∑ log Uκ,p(1) with terms tending to zero and probabilistically negligible tails gives full support [1,∞). Strict local power-mean monotonicity gives coupled Wκ<Wλ a.s.; dominated convergence yields endpoint continuity. For κ=2 the exact local factor is 1+1/(2p(p−1)); independent rational arithmetic verified local identities for six primes and seven exponents. No inference of absolute continuity or convergence rate.
residual_risks: Weak limits proved non-atomic, not Lebesgue absolutely continuous; no empirical rate or elementary distribution function.
